guidance.when: FEDERAL is an allowable namespace and the asset is property of the debtor.
guidance.procedure: Evaluate every applicable specific paragraph, then independently include 11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(5), which can protect any property. A dollar ceiling limits protection rather than eligibility. Thus a vehicle remains eligible under § 522(d)(2) above its cap, jewelry uses § 522(d)(4), and § 522(d)(5) remains an additional alternative even when a specific paragraph applies.
guidance.avoid_when: Do not use 11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(3) for an unlisted category such as a firearm or jewelry, do not omit a specific paragraph because value exceeds its ceiling, and do not repeat a citation.

scope_limits: Citations may justify EV or a shared rule; absence of an EC error among them does not prove the EC edit unjustified or legally false.
Cited-source outcome is the complete actual proposal, not the isolated operation; multiple operations and whole-wire stochastic changes may contribute.
Pooled current/past scores describe the fixed actual proposal only. They do not simulate a capacity-valid alternative publication or retrained policy, and cannot predict new-case effects.
Repeated teacher and component views are not independent cases. Complete-output support distinguishes native EC negative-asset ceiling effects; it does not replace the native primary metric.
